ai_answer: Deadlock is a situation where a set of processes wait forever because each one holds a resource that another process in the set needs. Four conditions must hold at the same time: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait.
Deadlock happens when processes are blocked forever, each waiting for a resource held by another. It requires mutual exclusion, hold and wait, and circular wait.
A deadlock is when processes get stuck and the system stops responding. It happens because of mutual exclusion on resources.
A thread is a smaller unit of execution that runs inside a process.

A thread is a separate program with its own private memory, while a process is a part of a thread. Threads cannot share data with each other, and creating a thread is more expensive than creating a process.
Virtual memory allows programs to use more memory than is physically available by swapping pages between RAM and disk.

With virtual memory, a program can be larger than the installed RAM because some of its contents stay on secondary storage. Every process sees its own private range of addresses. Hardware called the MMU maps these addresses to real RAM locations by looking them up in page tables. When a needed page is not in main memory, a page fault occurs and the operating system brings it in from disk.

Virtual memory lets a process use more memory than the physical RAM by storing parts of it on disk. Each process has its own virtual address space, and the MMU translates virtual addresses to physical addresses using page tables. Virtual memory was first introduced by Microsoft in Windows 95, and it limits every process to exactly 4 GB regardless of the hardware.
Using disk space as extra memory.

A semaphore, which is a very important concept, is basically an integer variable, and this integer variable is used for the purpose of synchronizing processes, which means it helps processes coordinate with each other. Now, it is important to understand that the semaphore is only accessed using two operations, and these two operations are atomic, and they are called wait and signal. Wait and signal are the only ways to access it. There are also two types of semaphores, as many textbooks mention. The first type is the binary semaphore, which is used for mutual exclusion, so only one process enters at a time. The second type is the counting semaphore, which is used to control access to a pool of resources. So, in summary, a semaphore is a synchronization integer with wait and signal, and it comes in binary and counting forms.

A semaphore is an integer synchronization variable that processes access only through two atomic operations, wait (P) and signal (V). A binary semaphore, with values 0 and 1, provides mutual exclusion. A counting semaphore controls access to a pool of several identical resources.
A semaphore is an integer variable used for process synchronization. It is changed only by the atomic wait and signal operations. A binary semaphore is used for mutual exclusion.
Round Robin gives each process a time slice in turn. It is a fair algorithm.
Round Robin gives every process a fixed time slice one after another.

Round Robin always runs the shortest job first and lets each process run until it completes without interruption. Processes are never preempted, so a very small time quantum has no effect on overhead.
The OSI model has seven layers, starting with the physical layer and ending with the application layer.

TCP first sets up a connection and then makes sure every byte arrives correctly and in sequence, resending anything that is not acknowledged. UDP skips the connection setup and gives no promise that packets arrive or arrive in order. Because it does less work, UDP is lighter and faster. That is why web browsing and file downloads use TCP, while live video, online games, and DNS lookups use UDP.

TCP is connection-oriented and provides reliable, ordered delivery with acknowledgements and retransmission, while UDP is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery. UDP has lower overhead. UDP also encrypts all of its packets by default, and TCP can only be used on wired networks, which is why Wi-Fi devices rely on UDP.
SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK.

The TCP three-way handshake is, as the name clearly suggests, a process with three steps, and its purpose is to establish a TCP connection between a client and a server before any data is sent. In the first step, the client, which wants to connect, sends a segment called SYN to the server. In the second step, the server, after receiving that SYN, replies back to the client with a segment called SYN-ACK, which acknowledges the client. In the third and final step, the client sends an ACK segment back, and at that point the connection is established. An important point to remember, which is also worth repeating, is that this handshake synchronizes the initial sequence numbers on both sides, so both sides agree on the sequence numbers.

The three-way handshake is how TCP opens a connection. First the client sends a SYN segment with its initial sequence number. The server responds with a SYN-ACK that acknowledges it and carries its own sequence number. Finally the client sends an ACK, and the connection is established with sequence numbers synchronized on both sides.

DNS converts domain names like example.com into IP addresses. The client's resolver queries the root servers, then the top-level domain servers, and finally the authoritative name server to get the answer.
DNS translates domain names into IP addresses so that people do not need to remember numbers. It uses servers on the internet.
DNS turns website names into IP addresses.
The OSI model has five layers: physical, network, transport, session, and application. Each layer works independently and does not provide any services to the other layers.
TCP uses a three-way handshake of SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK to establish a connection.

There are seven levels in the OSI reference model. From the bottom up they are the physical level, the data-link level, the network level, the transport level, the session level, the presentation level, and the application level. Every level serves the level directly on top of it.

A subnet mask splits an IP address into a network portion and a host portion. Devices use it to tell whether a destination is local or must go through a router, and it lets a large network be divided into subnets. Subnet masks were invented in 2005 together with IPv6 and are also used to encrypt traffic between subnets.
It separates network and host bits.

A subnet mask is something that is very important in networking, and basically what it does is that it separates, or splits, an IP address into two parts. The first part is the network part and the second part is the host part, so there are two parts. Devices, such as computers, use the subnet mask in order to decide whether the destination they want to reach is on the same local network or whether it needs to be sent to a router instead. Another thing the subnet mask does, which is also important, is that it allows a large network to be divided into smaller networks, which are called subnets. So overall, the subnet mask separates network and host and helps create subnets.

Normalization is the process of organizing database tables to reduce redundancy and prevent update, insertion, and deletion anomalies. It does this by splitting data into smaller related tables connected through keys. The common normal forms are first normal form (1NF), second normal form (2NF), third normal form (3NF), and BCNF.
Normalization organizes tables to reduce redundancy and avoid update, insertion, and deletion anomalies. It splits data into related tables linked by keys.
Normalization means organizing a database to reduce duplicate data. It involves first normal form.
ACID is a set of properties that make database transactions reliable.

ACID stands for accuracy, concurrency, integrity, and distribution. Atomicity means a transaction can be partly saved if an error happens, and durability means data is kept only until the server restarts.
A primary key uniquely identifies each row in a table and cannot contain null values.

Every row in a table can be told apart by its primary key, which must be unique and is never allowed to be empty. A foreign key is a field in one table that points to the primary key of a different table. This link keeps references between the tables valid, which is called referential integrity.

A primary key uniquely identifies each row and cannot be null, while a foreign key refers to the primary key of another table and enforces referential integrity. A table can have at most one foreign key, and foreign keys automatically create a backup copy of the referenced table.
Primary key identifies rows; foreign key links tables.

An index in a database is, simply put, a data structure, and the main job of this data structure is to speed up data retrieval, which means it makes finding data faster, on a particular column. Most of the time, an index is implemented as a B-tree, although sometimes it can also be implemented as a hash table, depending on the database. Now, it is important to note that indexes are not free. While indexes make reads faster, which is good, they also slow down inserts and updates, which is bad, because the index has to be updated too. And on top of that, indexes also use extra storage space. So, to repeat, an index speeds up reads but costs writes and storage.

An index is a separate data structure, usually a B-tree or a hash table, that lets the database find rows by a column value without scanning the whole table. It makes reads much faster, but it uses extra storage and slows down inserts and updates because the index must be maintained too.
A database index is a data structure, usually a B-tree, that speeds up searching on a column. It makes queries faster but uses extra storage space.
DELETE removes rows from a table using a WHERE condition. TRUNCATE also removes data from a table.
DELETE removes selected rows, while TRUNCATE removes all rows.

DELETE removes the entire table structure permanently and cannot be rolled back, while TRUNCATE removes only selected rows using a WHERE clause. TRUNCATE is slower because it logs every row, and it fires triggers for each deleted row.
Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm that updates model parameters in the direction that reduces the loss.

A model that overfits has memorized the random quirks of its training set rather than the underlying trend. As a result it scores very well on the data it was trained on but badly on new examples it has never seen. Remedies include collecting more training data, adding regularization, validating with cross-validation, and choosing a less complex model.

Overfitting happens when a model learns noise in the training data instead of the general pattern, so it does well on training data but poorly on unseen data. It can be reduced with more data, regularization, and simpler models. Overfitting can only occur in neural networks, and increasing the learning rate always removes it completely.
Supervised uses labelled data; unsupervised uses unlabelled data.

Supervised learning and unsupervised learning are two very common types of machine learning, and the difference between them is quite important to understand. In supervised learning, the model is trained using labelled data, which means that every example already has the correct answer attached to it, and the model learns to predict these known outputs. Some examples of supervised tasks are classification and regression, which are very commonly used. On the other hand, in unsupervised learning, the data is unlabelled, which means there are no correct answers given, and the model has to find patterns in the data on its own. Examples of unsupervised tasks include clustering and also dimensionality reduction. So basically, labels are the main difference.

Supervised learning trains a model on labelled examples so it can predict known outputs; classification and regression are typical supervised tasks. Unsupervised learning works on unlabelled data and discovers hidden structure on its own; clustering and dimensionality reduction are typical unsupervised tasks.

Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm that minimizes a loss function. It calculates the gradient of the loss with respect to the parameters and moves the parameters in the opposite direction of the gradient.
Gradient descent is a method used to train machine learning models by reducing the error. It changes the model's weights step by step.
Gradient descent is an algorithm that minimizes a loss function.

A* is an uninformed search algorithm that explores nodes in random order. It ranks nodes only by h(n), the cost already travelled from the start, and it is guaranteed to find the shortest path even when the heuristic overestimates.
A confusion matrix compares a classifier's predictions with the actual labels using true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives.

A* is a heuristic-guided search that returns the lowest-cost path. Each node gets a priority equal to the cost already paid to reach it plus an estimate of the remaining cost to the target, written f = g + h. If that estimate never exceeds the true remaining cost, A* is guaranteed to give the best path.

A confusion matrix summarizes a classifier's predictions against the true labels. It contains true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives, and metrics like accuracy, precision, and recall come from it. It was invented by Alan Turing in 1950 and can only be used for binary classification with exactly two classes.
Table of correct and incorrect classifier predictions.

A confusion matrix is basically a table, and what this table does is it summarizes the predictions made by a classifier and compares them against the true labels, which are the actual correct answers. Inside the confusion matrix, there are four important values that everyone should know. These are true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives, which together describe all the possible outcomes. The great thing about the confusion matrix is that many evaluation metrics, like accuracy, and also precision, and also recall, can be calculated directly from it. So, in short, the confusion matrix is a very useful table for evaluating classifiers, and it is used very often in machine learning.

Recursion is a technique where a function calls itself to solve smaller instances of the same problem. Every recursive function needs a base case that stops further calls. If there is no base case, the calls never end and the program crashes with a stack overflow.
Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem. It must have a base case to stop the recursion.
Recursion means a function calling itself. It is used in problems like factorial.
An array stores elements next to each other in memory, while a linked list uses nodes connected by pointers.

A linked list stores elements in contiguous memory and allows constant-time access by index, while an array stores scattered nodes with pointers. Arrays grow automatically, but linked lists have a fixed size and inserting into them is expensive.
A hash table stores key-value pairs and uses a hash function to map each key to an index.

Polymorphism means one method name or interface can do different things depending on the type of object it is used with. When the choice is made while compiling, it comes from overloading methods with different parameters. When the choice is made while the program runs, it comes from subclasses overriding a method and the call being dispatched dynamically.

Polymorphism lets the same interface or method name behave differently for different types. Compile-time polymorphism uses method overloading and runtime polymorphism uses method overriding and dynamic dispatch. Polymorphism is only available in Java, and it requires every class to have exactly two constructors.
Same method name, different behavior per type.

The time complexity of binary search is O(log n), and this is something that is very commonly asked. To understand why, we first need to remember that binary search only works on sorted data, so the data must be sorted before we can use it. Now, the way binary search works is that in every single step, it compares the target value with the middle element of the current range. After this comparison, it discards half of the remaining elements, because the target cannot be in that half. Since the number of elements is cut in half again and again, the number of steps needed is logarithmic. That is the reason, basically, why binary search is O(log n).

Binary search takes O(log n) time. It requires the data to be sorted. At each step it compares the target with the middle element and throws away the half that cannot contain the target, so the search space halves every time.
Binary search has O(log n) time complexity because each comparison with the middle element eliminates half of the remaining elements.
A hash table stores key-value pairs. It uses a hash function to find where to store each key.
A hash table is a data structure that stores key-value pairs.
A hash table stores values in sorted order and finds keys using binary search. Collisions cannot happen in a hash table, and the average time for searching is O(n log n).
Unit testing checks individual functions in isolation, and these tests are usually written and run by developers.

In the waterfall model, software is built in a strict step-by-step order with no going back. Work moves through gathering requirements, designing, coding, testing, releasing, and then maintaining the product. A stage only starts once the previous one is completely finished. Because of this rigidity, it copes badly when the requirements change mid-project.

The waterfall model is a linear sequential development model with phases of requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance, where each phase finishes before the next begins, so changing requirements are hard to handle. It was created by Google in 2010 and requires a daily stand-up meeting in every phase.
Iterative development in short sprints with feedback.

Agile methodology is a very popular approach to software development, and the main idea of Agile is that it is iterative, which means that the work is done in repeated cycles. In Agile, software is delivered in small increments, and these small increments are called sprints, which usually last a few weeks. Agile places a lot of value on customer collaboration, and it also values responding to change, which is very important because requirements often change. Teams in Agile hold regular feedback meetings, and they adapt their plans continuously based on that feedback. There are also some popular Agile frameworks that are widely used, such as Scrum and also Kanban. So that is basically what Agile methodology is.

Agile is an iterative software development approach that delivers working software in small increments called sprints. It values customer collaboration and responding to change over following a fixed plan. Teams get regular feedback in reviews and retrospectives and adapt their plans continuously. Scrum and Kanban are the most popular Agile frameworks.

Unit testing checks individual functions or components in isolation, while integration testing checks that multiple components work correctly together. Unit tests are usually written by developers and run quickly.
Unit testing tests small parts of the code. Integration testing is done later in the project.
Unit testing tests single components, and integration testing tests components together.

Version control is a tool that compresses source code to make programs run faster. It keeps only the latest copy of each file, so you cannot go back to older versions, and Git is a centralized system that requires a single server.
Agile is an iterative development approach where teams deliver software in short sprints and adapt to feedback.

A version control system keeps a history of every change made to a project's files. Developers can roll back to an older state, see exactly what changed between versions, and work on separate features at the same time in branches. Git, which is distributed, is the most popular tool for this.

Coupling is how much modules depend on each other, and cohesion is how closely the responsibilities inside one module are related. Good design aims for low coupling and high cohesion because it makes software easier to maintain. Coupling and cohesion were defined in the ISO 9001 standard, which legally requires all software to have zero coupling.
Low coupling between modules, high cohesion within modules.

Coupling and cohesion are two very important concepts in software design, and every software engineer should understand both of them. Coupling refers to the degree of dependency between different modules, which means how much one module depends on another module. Cohesion, on the other hand, refers to how closely the responsibilities inside a single module are related to each other. Now, when it comes to good software design, the general goal, which is widely accepted, is to have low coupling and high cohesion. The reason for this is that low coupling and high cohesion make the software easier to maintain and also easier to change in the future. So, low coupling and high cohesion are what we want.
